An artist finds a new home in China.

Spanish artist Jaume Ribalta has made a home in Jingdezhen, a Chinese city famous for pottery. His work brings together ideas from Spain and China. He grew up in a small town in Catalonia, where people have made pottery for a long time.

Ribalta began exploring art at eight, when he joined a small workshop. Later, he studied art and design in Barcelona. He learned to see pottery as more than making objects: it could connect drawing, painting and other kinds of art.

He came to China in twenty seventeen to teach. During his holidays, he traveled and learned about Chinese painting and calligraphy. He was especially interested in blue-and-white pottery. Learning from local artists helped him explore a new culture while developing his own work.
